title: LLMOps & Systematic AI Evaluation
description: Evaluate AI systems systematically in .NET using Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Evaluation, golden datasets, retrieval metrics, and regression testing.

data.text: Why LLMOps and Systematic Evaluation Are Non-Negotiable

In traditional software, deterministic unit tests verify that f(x) == y. But LLMs are probabilistic: a prompt tweak that improves answer quality on one edge case might secretly cause severe regressions across twenty other common questions. Furthermore, model upgrades (such as migrating from GPT-4o to o3-mini or fine-tuned weights) can alter reasoning styles, token outputs, and structured JSON reliability.

data.title: The Core Questions of LLMOps in .NET
data.text: Every production AI lead must be able to answer: 1) How do we prove a new prompt is objectively better? 2) Did switching models introduce subtle regressions? 3) Is our retrieval failing or is the LLM hallucinating? 4) How do we trace multi-step agent failures across tool calls? 5) How do we systematically investigate incorrect answers reported in production?
In RAG systems, you must measure retrieval performance independently from generation performance. If retrieval fetches irrelevant documents, no LLM can generate an accurate response.

rows: Percentage of ground-truth relevant documents retrieved in top-k results
Average of reciprocal ranks (1/rank) of the first relevant document
Evaluates ranking quality, giving higher weight to top positions
Percentage of claims in the generated answer directly supported by retrieved context
Degree to which retrieved chunks actually pertain to the user's question
Degree to which the final response directly addresses user intent

data.text: Microsoft provides Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Evaluation as a first-class NuGet package for evaluating AI models and RAG workflows directly within .NET test suites. It integrates with xUnit, NUnit, and CI/CD pipelines.

data.text: Tracing Failed Agent Runs with OpenTelemetry & .NET Aspire

When an agent fails or produces an incorrect answer across a 6-step loop, looking only at the final response makes debugging impossible. By emitting OpenTelemetry spans conforming to OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions, you can inspect:

data.title: Observability Tracing Checklist for AI Diagnostics
items: Exact input prompt and system instructions for every internal step
Raw tool-call names, JSON argument payloads, and return values
Token usage breakdown (input prompt tokens vs output generation tokens vs cached tokens)
Step-by-step latency showing whether bottleneck was database retrieval or LLM inference
Aspire dashboard visualization showing parent-child spans linking HTTP request -> Agent -> Tools -> LLM calls

data.text: Never evaluate prompts purely on intuition. Maintain a versioned JSON/CSV 'Golden Dataset' containing 100-500 representative questions with expected facts, required citations, and forbidden inaccuracies. When engineers open a pull request changing a prompt or model deployment, a GitHub Actions workflow executes the evaluation suite and posts a metric comparison table to the PR.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Prompt engineering without systematic evaluation is guesswork
Decouple retrieval metrics (Recall@k, MRR) from generation metrics (Groundedness, Relevance)
Use Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Evaluation for automated testing in standard .NET test frameworks
Trace multi-step agent tool calls using OpenTelemetry and .NET Aspire to debug failures
Automate evaluation gates in CI/CD to prevent quality, latency, and cost regressions
data.takeaway: LLMOps brings rigor to generative AI. By testing with Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Evaluation and tracing with OpenTelemetry, .NET developers ensure production AI features are measurable, auditable, and resilient to regressions.
